The evolution of amyloid β deposition was studied in 24 patients of different ages with Dutch-type hereditarily cerebral hemorrhage with amylodiosis (HCHWA).

in the Dutch-type hereditary cerebellar hemorrhage with amyloidoses, the amyloid-β deposits in the brain parenchyma have a heterogeneous morphology and that the distribution of the different types of plaques is age-related.

in HCHWA-D the parenchymal amyloid β ( Aβ) deposits are composed of heterogeneous mixtures of Aβ42 and Aβ40 and that Aβ42-positive clouds and fine/dense diffuse plaques are associated with Aβ42-positive granular deposits in glial cells, whereas Aβ42-positive dense/homogeneous plaures are associated with degenerating neurites and/or amyloid deposits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of amyloid beta (Aβ) deposits and the associated pathology in the brains of patients with Dutch-type heritable cerebral hemorrhage with cerebral amyloid angiopathy (HCHWA).
the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of AD and related disorders.
the evolution of amyloid β deposits (plaque) in the frontal cerebral coex of 24 patients with hereditary cerebral hemorrhages with amyloidosis, Dutch type (HCHWA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCHWA is a model of the evolution of plaques and that Aβx-43 (Aβ43) is a major component of the plaques.
Aβ42 is the main constituent of plaques, but Aβ40 is also present and may be involved in the formation of plaques.
Aβx- 42 immunoreactivity in plaques is not necessarily associated with amyloid fibrils, but rather with the early stages of plaque formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Aβ42 deposits in clouds, diffuse and coarse plaques, whereas Aβ40 deposits in diffuse and homogeneous plaques, and that Aβ40 is a more reliable marker for plaques with a core.
Aβ40 is not a marker for plaque maturation, and that Aβ42 and Aβ40 may be differentially involved in plaque evolution.

the Dutch type hereditary Cerebral Haemorrhage with Amyloidosis is a model for the development of amyloid plaques, which is characterized by the appearance of Aß42 positive plaques with a heterogeneous morphology (clouds, fine/dense plaques, and homogeneous plaures), which may become Aß40 positive plaques with the appearance of Aβ40.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Dutch mutation is not a single disease but a continuum of different phenotypes, with the same underlying pathology.
the plaque morphology in Dutch HCHWA is not only age-related, but also Aβ species-related.
plaque heterogeneity may reflect different stages of Aβ deposition.
